name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
desc: A 240-acre tropical garden in the middle of the city, built around a billion-year-old granite outcrop and its famous 1921 glass house.

name: Cubbon Park
desc: Three hundred acres of rain-tree canopy beside the High Court — the city's green lung and its best morning walk.

name: KR Market (City Market)
desc: A 1900 Roman-arcade market where Karnataka's flower, spice and banana-leaf trade still happens by hand. Closed Sundays.

name: Bull Temple, Basavanagudi
desc: A 16th-century Vijayanagara shrine guarding a 6.5-metre monolithic Nandi, with the leafy Bull Temple Garden around it.

name: Gandhi Bazaar Food Street
desc: Bengaluru's oldest eating lane — filter coffee, hot Mysore pak, obbattu and a hundred sweet shops within fifty metres.

name: Bengaluru Palace
desc: Indo-Saracenic towers, a wood-panelled Durbar Hall and a Teak Gallery — the Wodeyars' British-era statement on Vittal Mallya Road.

name: ISKCON Temple, Rajajinagar
desc: South India's largest ISKCON centre — white domes, evening aarti and the free vegetarian meal served every afternoon.

name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
desc: An all-teak, four-square, arch-heavy palace of the Tiger of Mysore, set in gardens beside the old Bengaluru Fort.

name: Vidhana Soudha
desc: 'Government Work is God's Work' — a vast Dravidian-modernist legislature front worth walking up at dawn for the light alone.

name: MG Road & VV Pur Food Street
desc: The city's spine at dusk: flower sellers under the metro flyover, then Bengaluru's oldest bakery lanes and dosha street off it.

name: Bug Rock Bouldering
desc: The city's own granite bouldering garden — 400 short problems on ancient rock, five minutes from Hebbal.

name: Nandi Hills
desc: A 4,800-ft ridge 60 km north of Bengaluru where the morning cloud inversion sits below you.

name: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
desc: Indo-Saracenic marble and granite, painted ceilings and 97,000 bulbs lit on Sundays — the Wodeyar seat of Karnataka culture.

name: Chamundi Hills
desc: A thousand steep steps (or a ten-kilometre drive) to Mysuru's tutelary goddess, with a monolithic Nandi halfway down.

name: Mysuru Zoo
desc: One of India's oldest and best-run zoos — 250 species inside a heritage garden next to the palace.

name: St. Philomena's Cathedral
desc: A 1936 neo-Gothic twin-spired cathedral, among the tallest in Asia, built by the Wodeyars for Mysuru's Catholic community.

name: Jagan Mohan Palace Art Gallery
desc: Rani Chennamma's palace holding the Veer Ranga Rao collection — Thanjavur paintings, bronzes and musical instruments.

name: Brindavan Gardens & KRS
desc: Terraced gardens laid out as a mandala in the spill channel of the Kaveri dam; the musical fountain runs after dark.

name: Devaraja Market
desc: Mysuru's 1850s market under iron trusses — flower garlands by the rope, turmeric, betel and banana-leaf meals.

name: Doddaganesha Rice Museum
desc: A heritage hall of two hundred rice varieties and folk artefacts, with a café serving forgotten millets and old recipes.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Somnathapura
desc: A 13th-century Hoysala temple on a star-shaped platform whose outer wall carries the famous eighteen-armed Narasimha.

name: Daria Daulat Bagh, Srirangapatna
desc: Tipu's teak-columned summer palace on the island town's river bend, with his battle paintings and his tomb nearby.

name: Sri Ranganatha Temple, Srirangapatna
desc: One of Karnataka's oldest Vaishnava shrines, on a Kaveri island; its temple car still leads the Mysuru festival calendar.

name: Abbey Falls
desc: A three-hundred-foot plunge through coffee and spice forest near Madikeri; the shaded road down is half the picture.

name: Madikeri Fort
desc: A 17th-century Kodava fort with a gun tower, a prison-church and a fine view line over the Western Ghats.

name: Abbey Coffee Estate Tour
desc: A working arabica estate where the picker walks you from cherry to cup — and pours the roast you just picked.

name: Kuddale Cheluveshwara Temple
desc: The Kodava clan deity's temple five kilometres from Madikeri, where the priest is a member of the community, not a Brahmin.

name: Sambalal View Point
desc: A quiet forest shoulder on the Madikeri–Kushalnagar road with a long drop into areca and evergreen below.

name: Mandlapatti Hill View
desc: A rock lip four thousand feet above the Kaveri valley — the famous photograph looks straight down three hundred metres.

name: Rlyang Rae Adventure & Coffee Estate
desc: An adventure-and-coffee campus above the Kaveri: ziplines, rope climbs and an estate café pouring the local roast.

name: Nisargadhama Island Grove
desc: A sixty-four-acre river island near Kushalnagar joined to the bank by a hanging rope bridge — bamboo grove, deer, Kaveri.

name: Talakaveri, Source of the Kaveri
desc: The spring in the Brahmagiri hills where the Kaveri is held to begin; the tula-sankramana fair floods the tank each October.

name: Bhagamandala Temple
desc: Where the Kaveri meets the Kannika and Sujyoti — a confluence temple with a panchakuti shrine and a famous free kitchen.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
desc: A forest camp on the Kaveri where you bathe and feed rescued elephants with a mahout beside you.

name: Kemmannugundi Hills
desc: A 4,700-ft former Maharaja's hill estate of lawns, shadowed trails and views into the Tunga valley.

name: Z Point Viewpoint
desc: A zig-zag forest track out to a shoulder over the Mysore plateau — fourteen bends, no railings, a lot of air.

name: Hebbe Falls
desc: A five-hundred-foot two-stage drop inside an isolated reserve; the last eight kilometres are a jeep-only laterite track.

name: Apsara Konje Falls
desc: A slim four-hundred-foot fall under the Kemmannugundi drive road, with a short rocky walk through shola to its pool.

name: Baba Budan Giri Trek
desc: The 5,600-ft peak where Sufi saint Baba Budan carried the first seven coffee beans into India — a real climb, with a dargah on top.

name: Annapoorneshwari Temple, Horanadu
desc: The Kaveri-bank goddess of food, whose free kitchen feeds thousands a day — any caste, any hour, no questions.

name: Sringeri Sharada Mutt
desc: Adi Shankara's first cardinal math on a rocky Kaveri bend — twelve centuries of learning, and the best vegetarian canteen in Malenadu.

name: Kudremukh Trek
desc: Karnataka's second-highest peak, a grass horse-face ridge at 3,400 ft; forest-department registration and a local guide are required.

name: Virupaksha Temple
desc: Hampi's living heart — a shrine to Shiva as Virupaksha running since the 7th century, still fed by daily donations and still going.

name: Vitthala Temple & Stone Chariot
desc: The Vittala complex's granite chariot and its musical pillars — Vijayanagara at its most ingenious.

name: Hazara Rama Temple
desc: The royal temple of Deva Raya I, whose outer walls carry a continuous Ramayana bas-relief frieze.

name: Achyutaraya Temple
desc: A finished, unshowy Vijayanagara temple in a boulder hollow, with a paved walkway running off towards the Hanuman hill.

name: Elephant Stables
desc: A vaulted Indo-Islamic hall where the emperors kept their war elephants — the domes still echo.

name: Queen's Bath
desc: A bulbous-cupola pavilion of pools and terraces for the imperial women — the empire's water engineering in one building.

name: Lotus Mahal
desc: A two-storey pink-granite pavilion of interlacing arches inside the walled Zenana enclosure — Mughal and Vijayanagara in one breath.

name: Matanga Hill Sunrise Trek
desc: A thirty-minute stepped climb to the best dawn view over the boulder field, the river and the temple town.

name: Anjaneya Hill (Hanuman's Birthplace)
desc: Seven hundred steep steps to the temple on the hill the Ramayana says Hanuman was born on. Go at six in the morning.

name: Sasiveka (Bringing of Seed) Rock Carving
desc: A giant stone measure on the Achyutaraya walk that once set the price of a measure of seed — Vijayanagara's public record-keeping.

name: Hampi Dargah
desc: The Sufi shrine of saint Tunga, five minutes from the Virupaksha gopura — Hampi's oldest proof of two faiths sharing one city.

name: Anegondi
desc: The older temple town across the Tungabhadra — a fort, a Narasimha shrine and empty cobbled lanes that never got the crowds.

name: Tungabhadra Dam, Hospet
desc: Sir M. Visvesvaraya's 1953 dam across the river — a garden drive, sunset over open water, and the gateway to Hampi.

name: Kodaganalli Coracle Crossing
desc: The round bamboo coracles that still run across the Tungabhadra below Anjaneyadri, as they have for six hundred years.

name: Badami Cave Temples
desc: Four Chalukyan shrines carved straight into a red sandstone cliff in the 6th century, with a thousand steps climbing to a fifth.

name: Banashankari Temple
desc: The 7th-century shrine of the Chalukya clan goddess, still crowded on the tenth day of the bonapuri fair.

name: Badami Agastya Teertha & Shivalaya Tanks
desc: Twin eleventh-century shrines on the embankment of the tank, mirrored at sunset with the cliff behind them.

name: Pattadakal Group of Temples
desc: A UNESCO World Heritage site of ten eighth-century Chalukya temples, where the Virupaksha holds a Sanskrit victory inscription.

name: Sangameshwara Temple, Pattadakal
desc: The largest temple at Pattadakal, its narrative panels answering a whole epic in stone.

name: Durga Temple, Aihole
desc: Apsidal, bell-shaped and eighth-century — the shrine that earns Aihole its name as the cradle of Indian temple architecture.

name: Meguti Jain Temple, Aihole
desc: A walled 634 CE Jain shrine on a rise above Aihole, carrying the famous court-poet's inscription of the Chalukyas.

name: Mahakuta Temple Group
desc: Pre-Chalukya shrines around a tank-lined hamlet ten kilometres from Badami, with an early Kannada inscription on a pillar.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
desc: Vishnu as Keshava, in a 1117 Hoysala temple whose east wall carries a madanika as finely carved as any in India.

name: Kotilingeshwara Temple, Belur
desc: A modern shrine whose compound walls are built with a claimed million small lingas, minutes from Belur's main temple.

name: Hoysala Temple, Belavadi
desc: A 1206 Hoysala temple in a village said to have held thirty-six shrines, with the style's finest lathe-turned pillars.

name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
desc: The largest Hoysala temple, twice Belur's size, its friezes running as a continuous stone narrative around twin shrines.

name: Parshvanatha Basadi, Halebidu
desc: One of three twelfth-century Hoysala Jain basadis facing a shared enclosure — quiet, un-restored and beautifully cut.

name: Halebidu Archaeological Museum
desc: Recovered Hoysala fragments, inscriptions and local coins across from the temple — the best twelve minutes to understand the carvings.

name: Gommateshwara, Shravanabelagola
desc: A fifty-seven-foot monolithic Tirthankara on a hilltop, carved in the 10th century; six hundred steps and a Jain town below.

name: Jog Falls
desc: The Sharavathi dropping 830 feet in four named cascades; the stairway to the base opens only when the release is on.

name: Jog Falls Upper Viewpoint
desc: The high lookout eight kilometres above the falls where the whole plunge comes into a single frame.

name: Magod Falls
desc: The Niagara of Karnataka — a 650-foot double horseshoe over the Bhadra, with a forest path down to the spray.

name: Bhadra Backwaters & River Road
desc: A quiet river road along the Bhadra reservoir — great hornbills in the trees and fishing boats at the bends.

name: Gokarna Main Beach
desc: A clean arc of sand where a temple town meets surf school — no night-glow, no casino, no jet skis within the bay.

name: Mahabaleshwara Temple, Gokarna
desc: One of the five Atalinga shrines of Indian legend, in the town the Ramayana says Ravana worshipped Shiva at.

name: Om Beach (Halla Beach)
desc: The bay that spells the sound Om from the headland above, with a rock in the middle of the shallows to climb.

name: Paradise Beach
desc: Reached only by a headland walk or a fishing boat — sand, coconut shade and no road at all.

name: Murudeshwara Temple & Gopura
desc: One of the tallest temple towers in the world beside a huge Shiva statue, with a beach walk directly underneath both.

name: Aghanashini Backwaters, Honnavar
desc: The areca-and-coconut-lined mouth of the Aghanashini — a country-boat cruise to the confluence, then crab curry on the bank.

name: Sri Krishna Mutt, Udupi
desc: Madhvacharya's 13th-century math, where you still watch the Krishna icon through the kanakana indi hole — and eat its famous prasade.

name: Malpe Beach
desc: Udupi's harbour beach and the boat point for St Mary's Island, with a headland that catches the last light.

name: St. Mary's Islands
desc: Hexagonal basalt columns — geologists' rain-drop stones — on a wild island six kilometres off Malpe, reached by boat.

name: Kapu Lighthouse & Beach
desc: An 1888 one-hundred-foot tower still lit above the Sarpangi river mouth, with a fishing beach on either side.

name: Maravanthe Beach
desc: The narrow sand bar where the Sauparnika river runs beside the sea and the highway climbs the Western Ghats behind it.

name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
desc: The goddess of the Kollur river on the Udupi–Karkala road, closed at midday because the deity is believed to sleep — and one of Karnataka's seven muktis.

name: Panambur Beach
desc: Karnataka's best-managed beach, eight kilometres north of Mangaluru, with lifeguards and a food row behind the sand.

name: St. Aloysius Chapel, Mangaluru
desc: A 19th-century Jesuit chapel painted ceiling to floor by Antonio Moscheni — called the Sistine Chapel of India.

name: Netravathi Estuary & Bolar
desc: The river mouth between two bridges where Mangaluru's port cranes, the lighthouse hill and the sea all sit in one view.

name: Kudroli Gokarnanatha Temple
desc: A carved laterite shrine in the middle of Mangaluru, older than the British city and the heart of the Dasara car festival here.

name: Talapaca Waterfalls
desc: Deep pools and a hanging rope bridge in the forest 50 km inland from Mangaluru — locals swim, the path is slick in monsoon.

name: Dharmasthala Kshetra
desc: A nine-hundred-year shrine where a Jain tirtha and Hindu deities share one courtyard, running the biggest free-food kitchen in south Karnataka.

name: Kukke Subramanya Temple
desc: Subramanya under the Subrahmanya hills, reached through forest — the serpent shrine of south Kannada.

name: Bandipur Tiger Reserve Safari
desc: The Mysuru–Gudalur half of a continuous tiger landscape: bamboo forest, a water-hole wait and a chance of a big cat.

name: Nagarhole National Park, Kabini
desc: The Kabini backwater edge of the reserve — elephant herds and deer by the hundred on the banks in the dry months.

name: Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple Hills
desc: A Ranganatha shrine on a 5,000-ft ridge between two rivers, with a trek and a safari buffer forest around it.
